overview: The Chola Empire was a maritime power that dominated southern India and Southeast Asian trade for over four centuries. Its lost-wax bronze sculptures, monumental temple architecture and naval expeditions represent the pinnacle of Dravidian civilization.

items.text: The Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur completed, one of India's greatest architectural achievements.
Chola bronze sculptures of Shiva Nataraja achieve perfection in the lost-wax technique.
A naval expedition launched against Srivijaya to protect Chola trade interests in Southeast Asia.
Merchant guilds organized international commerce across the Indian Ocean.
Advanced irrigation systems with tanks and canals supported intensive rice agriculture.
Shipbuilding and naval technology enabled overseas military expeditions.
The Great Living Chola Temples are UNESCO World Heritage sites.
Bronze casting techniques influenced art throughout Southeast Asia.

fall.text: The Chola dynasty declined and was absorbed by the resurgent Pandya kingdom.
